key_insight: MPS encoding makes non-local pseudopotentials practical in first-quantized quantum simulation by reducing Trotter-step circuit depth.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more scalable route to quantum chemistry and molecular dynamics on near-term quantum hardware, especially when pseudopotentials are needed to cut electron count and gate cost.
method: Encode the wave function with matrix product states (MPS) to represent non-local potential terms efficiently.
Construct a Trotter-step operator whose depth scales with local-potential degree, atom count, projector count, and bond dimension.
Compare against direct unitary decomposition using a 1D hydrogen ionization model under an ultrashort laser pulse.
evidence_signal: In the one-dimensional hydrogen atom ionization test, the proposed MPS encoding significantly reduced circuit depth compared with direct unitary decomposition.
watch_item: The approach still depends on MPS bond dimension and problem structure, so efficiency may degrade for strongly entangled or higher-dimensional systems.
paper_title: First-quantized quantum simulation with non-local potentials by matrix-product-state encoding
